leakage.confidence_note: I cannot see the harness's ctx.history semantics or ctx.actionable definition, but the code reads only history[-1] (described as the just-closed bar), accumulates per-session state solely from closed bars, uses session_open from the first bar's open at the time it is observed, and never touches the scorer, dataset, split, or calendar beyond ctx.session_end which is a known boundary.

reasons: Hypothesis match: developed hypothesis selects the continuation arm of the original 'continue or give back' question (outsized trend-aligned move with delta and volume confirmation), which is a member of the family the pre-registration named; code enters in the direction of the move (bar_direction == session_direction), matching the claim.

Economics do not hinge on costs: commission_paid_points = 76.8 / gross_pnl_points = 1022.75 = 7.5% of gross on train, and 17.2 / 195.5 = 8.8% on validation — net is positive in both splits and costs are not deciding the outcome.
Not a degenerate optimum: 384 trades over 384 sessions (one per session), avg holding ~96 minutes, turnover 2 contracts/session round trip — active, not maximising score by inactivity.

Per-trade edge (~2.46 points gross, 2.46 net after costs) is well above the ~0.2 point round-trip commission and would still clear a 1-tick NQ spread; the effect size is plausible for NQ at 5m scale with 1 contract.

Original hypothesis is economically plausible on its own: a session-level momentum continuation on NQ at 5m bars with ~1.5h holds is a standard, fill-tolerant claim and does not require sub-tick execution.
